hooks.prompt:
Condition: Claude may stop now. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

Answer ok:true (the condition is satisfied) unless the transcript CLEARLY shows one of the two violations below. Evidence that is missing, ambiguous, or in a part of the transcript that was cut off counts as no violation: answer ok:true.

If the hook input has "stop_hook_active": true, answer ok:true without checking anything else.

"This turn" means everything since the user's most recent typed message (not system reminders, tool results, task notifications or stop-hook feedback).

Violation 1: this turn Claude ran gh pr merge (without --auto), and either Claude's final message (last_assistant_message in the hook input) does not state that the merged PR's latest reviewer verdict was CLEAN and its CI green, or the transcript shows that verdict was not CLEAN or that one of its CI checks had failed. A merge whose final message names no CLEAN verdict is a violation even when no verdict appears anywhere.

Violation 2: this turn Claude opened a PR or pushed commits to one, and its final message says that work is finished or ready to merge, while the transcript shows no reviewer agent was started on the PR or re-asked about those new commits.

A violation counts however the final message ends: closing with a question, or saying it is waiting on something else, does not excuse it.

The project's review rule is one consolidated reviewer per PR, re-checking each new commit, with merges only on a CLEAN verdict and green CI. Per-file-type reviewers (ts-principal, qa-engineer, doc-expert, security-reviewer, python-principal, go-principal, architect) are never required; their absence is not a violation. Turns that shipped nothing, turns waiting on CI or a reviewer, and turns that ask the user something all satisfy the condition.

When you answer ok:false, the reason names the PR and the violation in one sentence.
